title: Welgemda Becomes First Approved Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Drug, Improving Walking Speed and Lung Function for One Rare Type
summary:
The Food and Drug Administration on Nov. 23 approved Welgemda (ribitol), an oral solution taken twice daily, for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9, according to the FDA's approval announcement. It is the first approved treatment for any form of limb-girdle muscular dystrophy.

title: CAR T offers new hope for stiff person syndrome
summary:
CAR T-cell therapy is linked with rapid and robust improvements across a number of disease-related measures in patients with stiff person syndrome (SPS), a “ground-breaking” new trial suggests.

The US study, which was funded by Kyverna Therapeutics and co-authored by company representatives, found that a single infusion of mivocabtagene autoleucel significantly improved walking speed 16 weeks later, with two-thirds of patients no longer requiring walking aids and benefits maintained at 24 weeks

title: Ekitna Plus Sunitinib Wins FDA Approval for Advanced GIST After Nearly Doubling Time Before Cancer Progression
summary:
The FDA on Nov. 24 approved Ekitna (bezuclastinib), from Cogent Biosciences, for use with sunitinib in adults with advanced gastrointestinal stromal tumors, or GIST, who have already been treated with imatinib, according to the FDA announcement.

In the phase 3 PEAK trial, people taking the combination went a median of 16.5 months before their cancer grew, compared with 9.2 months on sunitinib alone. Overall survival data are not yet mature, so it is not known whether patients will live longer.

title: FDA approves Welgemda, distributed by BridgeBio, for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 · Charted
summary:
The Food and Drug Administration on Nov. 23 approved Welgemda (ribitol), an oral drug for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9, an inherited muscle disorder that is rare, the agency said. The approval covers adults and pediatric patients who weigh at least 30 kg.
